Descending infection

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

An adult with a deep-neck abscess develops chest pain, persistent fever, and systemic deterioration despite initial therapy. Imaging shows infection tracking inferiorly from the neck into the thorax. Which complication most directly explains this progression?

  1. Descending mediastinitis
  2. Septic pulmonary embolism
  3. Parapneumonic empyema
  4. Acute pericarditis
  5. Pulmonary abscess from aspiration
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Descending mediastinitis

Deep cervical fascial planes can transmit infection into the mediastinum, causing a dangerous descending infection.

Understanding the options

Descending mediastinitis
Deep cervical fascial planes can transmit infection into the mediastinum, causing a dangerous descending infection.
Septic pulmonary embolism
This causes embolic pulmonary lesions, whereas the image describes direct inferior extension through neck tissues.
Parapneumonic empyema
An infected pleural collection is anatomically different from infection tracking into the mediastinum.
Acute pericarditis
Pericarditis does not explain direct spread along cervical fascial planes.
Pulmonary abscess from aspiration
An intrapulmonary abscess would not account for continuous neck-to-mediastinal extension.
